page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 60.0 GB of RAM, providing 7.5 GB per core. For acceleration, it includes a single NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 472 GB SSD, and the instance has a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between CPU and GPU performance. The Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 CPU exhibits weak single-core and multi-core performance, with stress-ng scores placing it in the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, with read-only large block bandwidth at 37.47 GB/sec. However, the integrated NVIDIA P100 GPU delivers strong results in machine learning tasks. LLM inference speed for prompt processing using a medium (7B) model reaches 316.69 tokens/sec (top 10%), and text generation for the same model achieves 42.77 tokens/sec (top 25%).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a legacy GPU-accelerated profile. While the CPU and memory subsystems show performance limitations compared to modern architectures, the inclusion of a dedicated 16 GB Pascal GPU and local SSD storage makes it a viable option for workloads that require GPU acceleration without the premium cost of newer-generation hardware. It is best suited for small to medium LLM inference, legacy machine learning workloads, and GPU-accelerated applications that do not heavily rely on high-performance CPU compute.
